question:
A generative application must automatically block model outputs that contain hate speech or self-harm content before they are returned to end users, without the application team writing their own text classifiers.

What should the team configure?

options.text: Configure the Foundry content safety filters on the model deployment, with severity thresholds set to block the disallowed categories before the response reaches the user.
Ask the model itself, via the system prompt only, to promise that it will never produce hate speech or self-harm content.
Add a client-side JavaScript word-blocklist that hides certain substrings in the browser after the response is already rendered.
Disable logging of model responses so that any problematic output is simply never reviewed.

explanation:
Built-in **content safety filters/guardrails** on the model deployment evaluate output against configured categories (hate, self-harm, violence, sexual) and severity thresholds, blocking or flagging disallowed content automatically before it is returned — exactly the "without writing your own classifiers" requirement.

**Why not the other options:**
- **A system-prompt promise** — Prompted instructions are guidance, not an enforcement mechanism; a model can still be steered around them, and there is no guaranteed blocking behavior.
- **A client-side blocklist after rendering** — Runs too late (the harmful content already reached the client) and is trivially bypassed by simply not filtering equivalent phrasing not on the list.
- **Disabling logging** — Removes visibility into what happened; it does nothing to prevent the harmful content from reaching the user and actively harms the team's ability to audit incidents.
category: Plan and manage an Azure AI solution
